Sparse indexed exact clocks propose removing CRN timestamp overhead under explicit batching and slowdown contracts For k positive formula-indexed rates lambda_i<=b, let q_i=1-lambda_i/b and acquire a certified q_star>=max q_i. Independent geometric extras P(G_i=m)=(1-q_i)q_i^m followed by H|G ~ Gamma(k+sum_i G_i, rate b) reproduce the full law of sum_i Exp(lambda_i). Geometric index skipping and thinning query rates only at candidates, with expected k q_star queries; an equivalent rational-envelope compound-Poisson route is provided. The source reports internal proof and separate internal reconstruction, not external correctness or a newly invented gamma-series identity.

For transformed CRN rates lambda_i=a binom(n+i g,o), fixed order o and growth g, k<=C sqrt(n), the acquired endpoint bound gives k q_star<=o g k(k-1)/(n-o+1)=O(1). The physical multiplier a is retained. A loose upper envelope can make the correction work linear. Random collision lengths need their actual second-moment/tail and content/clock independence argument, not merely E K=O(sqrt(n)). Rate-query count is not bit complexity or a bound on writing every timestamp.

Conditional on extras and H=h, A=k+sum G_i microphases have A-1 uniform interior order statistics. For u<h, one Binomial(A-1,u/h) draw W and J=max{j:j+sum_(i<j)G_i<=W} give the exact endpoint/prefix joint law by a sparse scan, with expected O(1) work under the explicitly supplied bounded-cost binomial primitive. A gamma/beta tree costs O(log k). Multiple cut times need joint counts or cached conditional splits; fresh independent cutoffs do not preserve a path law. Overshoot cost is unconditional per attempted block, not uniform under conditioning on rare overshoots.

The fixed-time integration assumes a fixed finite mass-action network/volume, correctly normalized transformed rates, an exact collision-batching content routine cost D(n_max), deterministic k=Theta(sqrt(n)) blocks, unconditional population bounds n_min,n_max before absorption (or a justified stopped-run contract), and transformed-to-active intensity slowdown <=rho. It gives expected work O(I_net+(D(n_max)+1)[1+rho E L_t/sqrt(n_min)]), where L_t counts original active reactions. Initialization, absorption-straddling blocks and compressed output are charged. Under the inspected matched source model D=O((2q)^o log(n_max+2)), fixed network, bounded slowdown and comparable populations, timestamp overhead no longer prevents the sqrt(n) batching improvement. Passive-event slowdown itself remains unresolved. An explicit reaction/timestamp history still costs linear output work.

Under the source binomial propensity convention, padding by delta identical catalysts needs k'=k V^delta/binom(m,delta); the inspected falling-factorial divisor omits delta!. This source-reported scoped counterexample does not refute the clock distribution, edit upstream mathematics or establish a historical-priority claim. Moschopoulos gamma-series, phase-type uniformization and ER-leap/HiER-leap gamma/simplex mechanisms are credited prior art. Candidate originality concerns sparse compilation and integration only.

Exact gamma/uniform/binomial random variates and real arithmetic are assumptions. Continuous exact-bit output, binomial decision near boundaries and a complete finite-bit CRN implementation remain OPEN; saved floating scripts and 77,370 exact cutoff inversions/120,000-trial diagnostics are producer checks, never rerun at intake. Existing N602 concerns a different finite-bit rare-clock interface and does not close these gates.
